details: Iran stated on Friday, May 30, 2026, that no final agreement has been reached with the United States regarding a ceasefire and its nuclear program, pushing back against US suggestions of a nearing deal. This ongoing uncertainty surrounding negotiations and the critical Strait of Hormuz continues to fuel volatility in global oil markets. Simultaneously, the US Treasury Secretary announced the seizure of $1 billion in Iranian cryptocurrency assets as part of Washington's economic pressure campaign against Tehran. The International Energy Agency, International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and World Trade Organization have warned that continued disruptions to shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz could increase risks to fuel security, market conditions, and broader economic resilience.
title: Iran Denies Final Deal with US; US Seizes $1 Billion in Iranian Crypto

details: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on May 29, 2026, approved the first US-listed Bitcoin perpetual futures contract and issued parallel relief allowing Coinbase to route American traders into global crypto derivatives markets. This is seen as a significant regulatory development that is expected to attract more institutional participation, enhance capital efficiency, and provide more regulated tools for hedging and managing exposure to digital assets, potentially expanding the US crypto derivatives market. This move could unlock access to roughly 80% of global perpetual markets.
title: US Regulator Greenlights Bitcoin Perpetual Futures, Boosting Institutional Access
